premises.text: Online and retail furniture shopping is risky because buyers cannot see how items will look in their own home
premises.evidence_span: hard to see how something that you choose online or even in a retail store will look in your own home

premises.text: Existing 3D home-modeling tools are too difficult, expensive, or slow for homeowners
premises.evidence_span: current solutions available are just too difficult for homeowners. They're too expensive, or they just take a long time

premises.text: A smartphone app captures wall photos plus IMU data so anyone can create a 3D model of their home in minutes
premises.evidence_span: allows anyone to create a 3D model of their own home with just a smartphone

premises.text: Users place catalog and favorite furniture in the model, measure, browse design boards, and collaborate with designers via links and sticky notes
premises.evidence_span: takes a sofa from the Crate and Barrel catalog and puts it in her living room

premises.text: Cloud GPU reconstruction from multi-image point clouds yields a WebGL geometrical and photorealistic room model quickly
premises.evidence_span: able to do this in a few minutes using GPU compute power on the cloud

premises.text: Connecting retailers to homeowners via the model increases sales, upsells, reach, and lowers returns

value.text: Homeowners shop for furniture with low risk by seeing pieces in a 3D model of their own home
value.evidence_span: disrupt the way we shop for furniture

secondary_value.text: Retailers make more money through better experience, upsell, reach, and fewer returns
secondary_value.evidence_span: our experience will make them more money

causal_links.evidence_span: breakthrough in technology and 3D model creation
your home becomes the ultimate showroom
providing the ideal shopping experience for homeowners

notes: Difficult/expensive/slow competitor pains folded as one pain-bundle in P2. Catalog place/measure/design-board/collaborate features folded into P4 as one room-shopping surface. Photorealism treated as performance detail of P5 reconstruction. Named retailer deal treated as traction evidence for P6 mechanism, not a separate premise. Anti-template note: D1/D2/D3 resemble need/product/channel but transcript separately revises visualization problem, capture+shop product, and retailer connection economics.
